A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Quartet study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, appendices and checklists are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original C4 training results, scaling-law fits, gradient analyses, downstream evaluations, GPU timings and appendix post-training quantization results.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical results and reports revised quantization comparisons and additional scaling-law extrapolation evidence.

M1.justification: Quartet replaces stochastic rounding with round-to-nearest for both backward GEMMs' operand quantization. Sections 4.3–4.4 and Algorithm 1 change this core gradient-estimation component while retaining the QuEST forward pass, Hadamard transforms, masks and rescaling factors.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4, HellaSwag, WinoGrande and ARC-Easy, alongside the same prefill and post-training quantization tasks. The larger-model extrapolation checks change model configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 2 adds QuEST alongside SR AbsMax and RTN AbsMax in the gradient-depth and backward-only loss comparisons; QuEST previously appeared in Table 2. The main Table 3 comparators and appendix QuaRot baseline remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 2(c) extends the comparison to 200M models, and appendix Figure 6 adds 430M/800M extrapolation checks beyond the retained 30–200M fitting grid. Tables 4–5 retain their settings. Table 2 drops its explicit 800-tokens/parameter qualifier without explaining whether efficiency estimation changed.

E4.justification: The central backward-quantization analysis is substantially revised: Figure 2 adds QuEST and replaces the earlier training-duration crossover with evidence favoring RTN throughout the tested budgets. Appendix A.3 also adds larger-model extrapolation checks; runtime-breakdown and PTQ analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2 already contains shaded bands in v3. V4 adds no run counts, experimental seed information, uncertainty definitions or significance tests; the new shaded extrapolation regions are not uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Table 2 reverses the reported backward-efficiency ranking: SR/RTN values change from 0.85/0.83 to 0.88/0.93, supported by revised Figure 2 findings. Figure 1's optimal-precision regions, Table 3 losses and efficiency entries, and appendix fit errors also change. Quartet's revised losses accompany its changed backward procedure, so they do not establish a same-method performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation 1, the parameter/data-efficiency formulation, the misalignment definition and the unbiased-rescaling equation remain unchanged. The empirical correction and algorithm revision introduce no new theorem, proof or formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the headline claims: a scaling-law comparison framework and native MXFP4 training that can optimize accuracy versus computation using fast Blackwell kernels. The backward-rounding correction does not redefine those stated contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 rejects v3's recommendation of SR for long runs, including the crossover near D/N=400, attributing that conclusion to an implementation bug. V4 instead favors RTN's balance of error and magnitude misalignment. Section 6 also removes the limitation specifically tied to stochastic-rounding hardware support.

D1.justification: New Figure 3 explicitly documents BF16 activations and gradients, FP32 weights, and dequantization/transpose paths. These expand implementation disclosure; the hyperparameter tables, kernel description, compute estimates and Quartet/QuTLASS access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds FP4 All the Way as concurrent work and positions Pretraining Large Language Models with NVFP4 and Tetrajet-v2 as extensions of Quartet. This is a limited addition of three references and a short positioning passage.

P1.justification: V4 locally rewrites Sections 4.3–4.4, retitles the third ingredient, moves Algorithm 1 into new Appendix A.1, and updates related work, acknowledgments and an affiliation. The overall narrative and section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds a computation-flow diagram, relocates Algorithm 1, revises Figure 2's axes and legends, and marks extrapolation in the scaling-fit plot. Other plots and most table layouts are retained, with subsequent figure and appendix renumbering.

improvement.justification: V4 identifies the implementation bug behind v3's erroneous long-run SR recommendation, revises Table 2 and Figure 2, and updates Algorithm 1 accordingly. Correcting the empirical premise used to select a central method component substantially improves scientific reliability. The extrapolation checks and computation diagram provide additional support; the decisive benefit is the correction, rather than the small loss changes.
